messages.content:
Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Please post a concise routing summary to #helio-start-ops for these current Helio Start authority-readiness cases: HS-801 — verified yes; HS-802 — no; HS-803 — not sure. Identify what happens next for each case and briefly name the readiness confirmation being applied.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "send_slack_message", "arguments": {"channel": "#helio-start-ops", "message": "Authority-readiness routing (confirmation: can you or an available owner perform the owner-level permission or network-allowlist action required by your selected connector? Track this separately from Helio admin proof and connector authentication.)
• HS-801 — Verified yes: record external authority as verified and continue the normal eligibility checks.
• HS-802 — No: keep pending and route to Customer Success before admission; hold setup prompts.
• HS-803 — Not sure: keep pending and route to Customer Success before admission; hold setup prompts."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_109_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The message must briefly and accurately identify the separate authority-readiness confirmation as whether the applicant or an available owner can perform the selected connector’s required owner-level permission or network-allowlist action in the setup or pre-setup context. Semantically equivalent wording is acceptable; the literal phrase “selected for first-week setup” is not required. The message must not conflate this confirmation with Helio admin proof, connector authentication, or another proof.

The message clearly identifies HS-801 (verified yes) as permitted to continue, and clearly identifies both HS-802 (no) and HS-803 (not sure) as requiring routing to Customer Success before admission. Missing, swapped, or contradictory outcomes must fail.", "value": {"channel": "#helio-start-ops", "message": "Authority-readiness routing (confirmation: can you or an available owner perform the owner-level permission or network-allowlist action required by your selected connector? Track this separately from Helio admin proof and connector authentication.)
• HS-801 — Verified yes: record external authority as verified and continue the normal eligibility checks.
• HS-802 — No: keep pending and route to Customer Success before admission; hold setup prompts.
• HS-803 — Not sure: keep pending and route to Customer Success before admission; hold setup prompts."}}]}

{"results":[{"check_id":"riley_109_02","passed":true,"reason":"The message defines the confirmation as whether “you or an available owner [can] perform the owner-level permission or network-allowlist action required by your selected connector” and explicitly says to track it separately from “Helio admin proof and connector authentication.” It permits HS-801 to “continue the normal eligibility checks” and routes both HS-802 and HS-803 “to Customer Success before admission.”"}]}
